title: Securing Agents with Open Standards — Bobby Tiernay and Kam Sween, Auth0
talk_summary: Auth0 engineers describe identity/access patterns for agents: per-user short-lived tokens via token exchange instead of shared static API keys, fine-grained authorization enforced at the RAG retrieval layer, and CIBA (client-initiated back-channel authentication) to get explicit user approval for high-risk agent actions. The demo is a TypeScript CLI trading agent that mints user-scoped tokens and pushes an approval notification before executing a trade.

takeaways.technique: Per-agent scoped credentials instead of shared static keys
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents request short-lived, narrowly scoped tokens from a backend/token vault rather than reading a shared API key from an env var, so each action is attributable and rotatable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an agent calling an API using a shared uh key pulled from an environmental variable... that key probably gets reused across users, environments

takeaways.technique: Enforce authorization at retrieval layer, not in the LLM
takeaways.what_they_do: For RAG, access decisions are made before data reaches the model, at the retrieval layer, rather than trusting the agent/LLM to filter what it should see.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You don't want the agent deciding access inside your LLM. You want that enforced much earlier at the retrieval layer

takeaways.what_they_do: Sensitive tool calls pause and dispatch an out-of-band approval request describing exactly what the agent wants to do; execution resumes only on approval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this agent tried to do this action, which in this case is purchasing 10 shares of something on your behalf. Would you like to approve

takeaways.technique: Bind agent sessions to a durable user/context identity
takeaways.what_they_do: The runtime binds each session to a specific user identity so actions are attributable and traceable after the fact.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to define the context and bind it to a particular thread for this particular session
